headline: Monitor Tidal Schedules and Seasonal Ferry Bookings
reservation: While entry to most public coastline views is open, specific sites like Joggins Fossil Cliffs or Burntcoat Head Park may require pre-booked guided tours for shore access. Commercial ferry crossings between Nova Scotia and New Brunswick are essential for certain itineraries and frequently sell out; verify schedules and reserve via the official ferry operator well in advance.

days.title: Fossils and Tides of the Glooscap Trail

stops.name: Joggins Fossil Cliffs
stops.detail: Observe exposed layers of Carboniferous history where the world's highest tides reveal prehistoric remains.

stops.name: Cape d'Or Lighthouse
stops.detail: Witness the dramatic tidal rips where the currents of the Minas Channel create visible maritime turbulence.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; conditions vary with coastal fog.
days.note: Shoreline access is strictly dependent on the twice-daily tidal retreat; consult local tide tables before descending.

days.title: Minas Basin Low Tide Explorations

stops.name: Burntcoat Head Park
stops.detail: Walk on the ocean floor at the site of the highest recorded tides in the world during the low tide window.

stops.name: Shubenacadie River
stops.detail: Watch for the tidal bore, a literal wave of water that flows upriver as the tide turns.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; heavy tractor traffic common in agricultural zones.
days.note: The red mud of the basin is extremely slippery; stick to established paths near the cliffs.

days.title: Acadia Region and Orchard Vistas

stops.name: Grand-Pré National Historic Site
stops.detail: Explore the dykelands created by 17th-century Acadians to manage the Fundy tides for farming.

stops.name: Cape Split Provincial Park Reserve
stops.detail: Follow the trail to the tip of the peninsula for a panoramic view of the bay's massive water volume.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; local winery traffic can slow regional roads.
days.note: Cape Split involves a significant walk; allow ample daylight to return before dusk.

intel.title: The Rule of Twelfths
intel.text: The water level changes most rapidly during the third and fourth hours of the cycle. Plan to be at shore locations at least one hour before the predicted low tide.

intel.title: Public Wharf Access
intel.text: Many wharves in the region are active commercial fishing hubs. Yield to working vehicles and be aware that ladders are for emergency use only.

intel.title: Parrsboro Supply Point
intel.text: Fuel is reliable in Parrsboro and Truro, but becomes scarce along the coastal Route 209 toward Advocate Harbour. Fill tanks before venturing into the more remote segments of the Glooscap Trail.

intel.title: Coastal Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect intermittent cellular service along the cliffs and in the deeply recessed bays. Download offline maps and tide schedules while in the major gateway towns.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking at Cape Split is limited and often fills during autumn weekends. Arrive early or visit mid-week to avoid overflow conditions on the narrow access roads.

plan.arrival: Pick up rentals at Saint John or Halifax; stock supplies in Truro before heading to coastal rentals or campsites.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for main routes; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved coastal access roads.
plan.goldenHour: Cape d'Or provides an elevated westward view over the Minas Channel, with colors shifting based on the coastal haze.
